newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA NAME AUSTRALIA'S YARDLEY AS NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA NAME AUSTRALIA'S YARDLEY AS NEW COACH.

text.p: Former Australian test spinner Bruce Yardley was named on Friday as Sri Lanka's new cricket coach.

Yardley, who played 33 tests for Australia, was highly recommended by former test greats South African Tony Greig and New Zealander Richard Hadley, Sri Lanka cricket board president Upali Dharmadasa told reporters.
Yardley is due in Sri Lanka in late January to replace departing coach Dav Whatmore, a former Australian test player who quit Sri Lanka to join English county side Lancashire.
The appointment ends a two-and-a-half month international search for a new coach for the World Cup champions.
Dharmadasa said Yardley's first task would be to prepare the team for the test tour of New Zealand early next year.
Yardley's last test for Australia was in the Sri Lankan hill town of Kandy in 1983, when he helped to bowl the visitors to victory with an eight-wicket haul.
Whatmore, a Sri Lankan by birth who emigrated to Australia, returned to Colombo in June 1995 to coach the team.
